I've switched to the New-Project Entry. Before I write any roadmap text, here are the outcomes, tracks and costs for you to rank and confirm.

**Roadmap file:** `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md`. The name comes from the spec's filename, so you don't need to pick one.

## Outcomes (unranked; candidates from the spec's R1–R11)

| # | Outcome (what you get) | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A canonical filing-index catalog in Parquet for a range of archived quarters you choose | R1, R3 | Requests are cheap: about one index file plus one listing per quarter, so even 100 quarters is a few hundred requests, about 2 minutes at 3 req/s. The data volume is not known yet; it depends on the range, which the spec leaves open (§4.8). The probe below would settle the size per quarter. |
| O2 | That catalog kept current from daily indexes, catching up after missed runs and across quarter boundaries | R2 | Small: about 250 daily files a year, about one listing and one download per business day. |
| O3 | Stored source bytes reprocessed after a parser change, with no new SEC download | R5, R6 | Storage: the raw bytes are kept forever, so it equals O1's volume plus about 250 daily files a year. |
| O4 | Weekly re-reads of quarterly indexes that apply additions and field changes on their own, and hold any removal until you approve it against the source's exact hash | R7, R10 | Your time: one approval per closed-quarter candidate that removes records. How often that happens is not known; only running it will tell. |
| O5 | Readers only ever see complete quarter datasets, reached through one active pointer per quarter | R9 | No material cost. |
| O6 | All SEC traffic shares one request budget (3 req/s, one collector at a time), however many workers run | R8 | No material cost. It caps throughput, but O1's request count makes that cap irrelevant. |
| O7 | Unattended scheduled operation on Azure: orchestration, jobs, storage, alerts, runbooks and rollback | R4, R11 | Azure dollars and your setup time are not known. The first Azure stage would measure them. |

R5 (shared code across backfill, daily and reconciliation) and R11 (default values need review before they change) are rules for how the work is built, not outcomes in themselves. I've attached them to O3 and O7. They would bind every stage rather than stand as stages of their own.

## Proposed tracks

- **Track A — Filing-index catalog (O1–O6), known progression.** It runs locally against real SEC indexes.
- **Track B — Azure operation (O7), known progression.** It depends on Track A's code.

I split them because the catalog is usable without Azure. Also, the ADR that chooses Azure is still *Proposed*, and spec §9 names an alternative (a schedule-only container deployment). Keeping Track B separate means Track A doesn't wait on that decision.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`).
- A uv workspace with four packages. The spec only gives `sec-edgar-ingest` a role (§4.9); the other three (`-client`, `-download`, `-index-ingest`) have none in the spec.
- Azure as the platform, per the ADR, but the ADR is Proposed, not accepted.

## Optional probe

To firm up O1's volume, I could fetch one `full-index` `index.json` listing and check the size of one quarterly `master.idx`. That is two or three requests. The SEC requires an identifying User-Agent, so I would only run this if you say yes and give me the name and contact email to send.

## One request

Please:

1. Rank the outcomes within each track.
2. Rank the two tracks against each other.
3. Confirm or change the tracks and their kinds (and whether Azure should be its own track at all).
